detailed_description: The Chinese Converter changes text between Simplified and Traditional Chinese using an in-page character mapping. Paste Chinese text, choose the conversion direction, review the converted output, and copy the result. It is useful for quick interface labels, short messages, and content drafts. The current browser tool focuses on character-level conversion and does not rewrite regional vocabulary, punctuation style, or idiomatic wording, so important publishing work should still be reviewed by a fluent reader.
usage_steps: Paste the Chinese text you want to convert.
Click Convert to Traditional or Convert to Simplified.
Review the converted output in the result box.
Check names, regional terms, and punctuation manually.
Copy the converted text when it looks right.
Clear the form before starting a new conversion.
usage_examples: Convert Simplified Chinese UI labels to Traditional Chinese for a mockup.
Convert Traditional Chinese text to Simplified Chinese for a draft note.
Normalize short Chinese snippets before sharing them with a teammate.
Quickly compare how common characters change between the two writing systems.

faqs.question: Does it translate Chinese into another language?
faqs.answer: No. It converts between Simplified and Traditional Chinese characters; it does not translate Chinese into English or another language.

faqs.question: Will it adapt regional vocabulary?
faqs.answer: No. The tool focuses on character conversion and does not rewrite regional wording, idioms, or terminology.

faqs.question: Can I use it for final publication?
faqs.answer: Use it as a fast draft helper, then review important text manually because character conversion cannot catch every language nuance.

faqs.question: Does it upload my text?
faqs.answer: The visible conversion runs in the browser page and does not require account login.

faqs.question: Why did some characters stay the same?
faqs.answer: Many Chinese characters are identical in Simplified and Traditional forms, so they do not change during conversion.
